data.title: Ryde Group Ltd Announces Non-Binding Term Sheet for Proposed Minority Investment in Multi Genius Limited and MOU on Technology Collaboration
data.description:
SINGAPORE, SG / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Ryde Group Ltd (NYSE American:RYDE) ("Ryde" or the "Company"), a leading technology platform for mobility and quick commerce headquartered in Singapore, today announced that it has entered into a non-binding term sheet with Golden Concord Group Limited in relation to a proposed acquisition of a minority interest in its subsidiary Multi Genius Limited ("MGL").

Separately, Ryde has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding ("MOU") with GCL Digital Technology (Holdings) Limited ("GCL Digital"), a subsidiary of MGL, to explore potential technology collaboration.

The announcement follows Ryde's previously unveiled Ryde 2.0 transformation plan, which includes exploring new opportunities to strengthen the Company's technology capabilities and support long-term growth.

MGL, through its subsidiaries, is engaged in the development of an energy-backed digital infrastructure platform with a focus on artificial intelligence ("AI") and high-performance computing ("HPC") technologies.

Under the indicative non-binding term sheet, Ryde is evaluating the potential acquisition of a minority equity interest in MGL, with an indicative aggregate transaction value of up to US$18 million. The final transaction structure, form and amount of consideration, valuation and other terms remain subject to due diligence, independent valuation, negotiation and definitive documentation.

The proposed investment forms part of Ryde's broader Ryde 2.0 strategy of selectively exploring partnerships and investments that could strengthen the Company's long-term technology capabilities. Ryde believes that advances in AI, computing infrastructure and cybersecurity may create opportunities to enhance its technology platform and support potential new areas of growth.

Separately, under the MOU with GCL Digital, the parties intend to explore potential collaboration across three areas: cybersecurity services, GPU computing infrastructure, and data centre operations and maintenance. The parties may also explore other mutually beneficial opportunities relating to AI, high-performance computing and digital infrastructure.

The MOU does not obligate either party to purchase, supply or procure any minimum quantity of hardware, infrastructure capacity or services, and any future commercial engagement would be subject to separate agreements.

The proposed investment in MGL and any potential procurement or technology collaboration under the MOU are being evaluated independently, and neither arrangement is conditional upon the other.

"Innovation has always been central to Ryde's long-term strategy," said a spokesperson for Ryde. "As we advance Ryde 2.0, we are exploring opportunities to strengthen our technology capabilities and participate selectively in emerging areas such as AI and digital infrastructure. Our engagement with MGL and GCL Digital reflects this approach, while maintaining a disciplined evaluation process focused on creating long-term shareholder value."

"We welcome Ryde's interest in Multi Genius and the opportunity to explore broader technology collaboration with GCL Digital," said Yang Yong, Director of GCL Digital Technology (Holdings) Limited. "We look forward to working with Ryde as the parties evaluate potential opportunities across AI computing infrastructure, cybersecurity and data centre operations."

The parties intend to undertake mutual due diligence over the coming months. As part of this process, Ryde intends to conduct comprehensive legal, financial, tax and regulatory due diligence on MGL, together with an independent valuation of MGL. Completion of the proposed investment will be subject to each party being satisfied with the results of its due diligence, the negotiation and execution of definitive binding agreements, receipt of the respective board and internal approvals, satisfaction of applicable regulatory and stock exchange requirements, and other customary closing conditions.

As at the date of this announcement, the proposed transaction remains indicative and non-binding, and no definitive acquisition agreement has been entered into. There can be no assurance that any definitive agreement will be executed or that the proposed transaction will ultimately be completed.

About Ryde Group Ltd

Ryde is a super mobility app founded in Singapore and recognised as the world's FIRST on-demand carpooling app since 2014. As a publicly listed company on the NYSE American, Ryde is reimagining the way people and goods move around by offering a full suite of services, including carpooling, private hire, taxi, and delivery. What distinguishes Ryde is its commitment to empowering private-hire and taxi partners by taking 0% commission, ensuring that drivers retain more of their hard-earned earnings. For more information, please visit https://rydesharing.com/.

About Multi Genius Limited

Multi Genius Limited ("MGL") is a technology-focused company engaged, through its subsidiaries, in the research and development of energy-backed digital infrastructure platforms. With a focus on artificial intelligence ("AI"), high-performance computing ("HPC") and next-generation digital infrastructure, MGL aims to support the growing demand for reliable, scalable and energy-efficient computing solutions. The company seeks to advance the integration of energy resources and computing technologies to support the evolving needs of the global digital economy.

data.title: ShareBuilder 401k Adds Fully Digital Loans to its Solo 401(k) Saver, Giving Self-Employed Access to Their Own Money
data.description:
ShareBuilder 401k Adds Fully Digital Loans to its Solo 401(k) Saver, Giving Self-Employed Access to Their Own Money

Owners can borrow half their vested balance up to $50,000 from pre-tax and/or Roth savings with no credit check, and repay the interest back to their own account

ShareBuilder 401k today announced that participant loans are now available in its Solo 401(k) Saver plan. Self-employed business owners can apply for a loan from their own retirement account entirely online, with no paperwork, no credit check and no lender approval.

Freelancers, consultants and other self-employed people don't have an employer safety net. When an unexpected expense comes up, or a bank won't lend on reasonable terms, many feel they have to choose between expensive debt and a taxable early withdrawal. A 401(k) loan offers another option. Owners borrow from their own savings and repay themselves over time. As long as the loan is repaid on schedule, it is not taxed and carries no early-withdrawal penalty.

“Self-employed people work hard to build their savings, and they shouldn't have to give up access to that money to save for retirement,” said Stuart Robertson, CEO of ShareBuilder 401k. “With a Solo 401(k) loan, you're borrowing from yourself. There are no bank or no credit checks, and the interest goes back into your own account, not to a lender. It's your money, and now there's a simple, digital way to put it to work when an urgent situation comes up, and you need it.”

How it works

  • Borrow from your own account. Owners can borrow up to 50% of their vested balance, to a maximum of $50,000, subject to IRS limits.
  • Pre-tax and Roth balances both qualify. Borrowers choose which sources to borrow from (or both), and repayments go back to those same sources.
  • Pay yourself back. The loan carries a fixed interest rate, and each repayment, including interest, is credited to the borrower's 401(k) account. It helps to offset the time the money isn't invested.
  • Fully digital. Owners apply online, and repayments are automatically withdrawn each month from their personal bank account over a term of up to five years.
  • Pay it off anytime. Owners can pay off the full loan early, online, with no prepayment penalty.

Two ways to build access

Owners can build their Solo 401(k) balance over time through contributions and borrow if needed. They can also roll eligible money from a former employer's 401(k) or an IRA into their ShareBuilder Solo 401(k) Saver account. IRS rules don't allow loans from IRAs, so for many savers, a Solo 401(k) is the only way to borrow from their retirement money. Rolled-in money typically becomes available to borrow once it settles in the account.

ShareBuilder 401k built loans into its Solo 401(k) Saver, so owners don't have to choose between saving for retirement and accessing their money in a pinch.

Borrowing responsibly

A 401(k) loan isn't free money, and it's not right for everyone. Borrowed money isn't invested while the loan is outstanding. If payments are missed and not made up in time, or if the plan is terminated while a loan is outstanding, the unpaid balance can become a taxable distribution. Borrowers under age 59½ may also owe a 10% additional tax on a deemed distribution. ShareBuilder 401k encourages owners to review the loan terms, fees and repayment schedule before borrowing.

Loans are available now to ShareBuilder Solo 401(k) Saver account holders. To learn more, visit www.sharebuilder401k.com.

About ShareBuilder 401k

ShareBuilder 401k is a leading digital provider specializing in low-cost, all-ETF retirement products for the self-employed and small businesses. Founded in 2005 and serving over 6,500 businesses nationwide, ShareBuilder 401k is a pioneer in index-based 401(k) plans, digital quoting, and investment management (ERISA 3(38)) services. The company is dedicated to closing the retirement savings gap by providing cutting-edge technology, transparent pricing, and quality education to business owners of all sizes.

data.title: Enel Buys Portfolio of U.S. Solar Plants From energyRe
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Enel agreed to buy a portfolio of solar plants in the U.S. from clean energy infrastructure developer energyRe, part of a strategic plan to grow generation capacity from renewable sources.

The Rome-based energy company said Friday that the plants, located in South Carolina, have a total installed capacity of 317 megawatts and an expected average annual production exceeding 540 gigawatt-hours.

Following completion and once the plants are in service, Enel expects the deal to boost its annual group earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization by around $30 million, while its total North American installed capacity of 13.5 gigawatts will come entirely from renewable sources.

Acquisition terms weren't disclosed, but Enel said that coupled with the costs of bringing the plants into service, it expects the deal to have an impact on group net financial debt of around $255 million.

Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

data.title: Holland America Line's 2028-2029 Asia Cruise Season Blooms with Cherry Blossoms and Five New Ports
data.description:
Holland America Line's 2028-2029 Asia Cruise Season Blooms with Cherry Blossoms and Five New Ports

Holland America Line's 2028-2029 Asia Cruise Season Blooms with Cherry Blossoms and Five New Ports

PR Newswire

SEATTLE, Nov. 20, 2026

Eurodam's first Asia season features new destinations, more time ashore and opportunities to experience Japan during its famed cherry blossom season

Key Takeaways:

  • Eurodam makes its Asia debut with five new ports, expanding Holland America Line's 2028-2029 season across Japan, South Korea, China, Taiwan, the Philippines and Southeast Asia.
  • More time ashore and Japan's cherry blossom season deepen the destination experience, with overnight stays and late-night departures across 14 ports, plus spring sailings timed to give guests opportunities to see the famed blooms.
  • A new 27-day Coffee, Tea & Spice Route Legendary Voyage expands longer exploration of the region, visiting 13 ports across seven countries and bringing Asia's culinary traditions on board through destination-inspired experiences.

SEATTLE, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Holland America Line announced its 2028-2029 Asia cruise season, adding five new ports across Japan, Taiwan, Brunei and the Philippines to a wide-ranging collection of cruises throughout the region. Aboard Eurodam, making its Asia debut, cruises explore Japan, South Korea, China, Taiwan, the Philippines and Southeast Asia.

 Five new ports, more time ashore and Japan's cherry blossoms highlight Holland America Line's 2028-2029 Asia season.

Sailing from September 2028 through May 2029, the season features itineraries ranging from 11 to 27 days, with departures from Tokyo, Japan; Hong Kong, China; and Singapore. Standout cruises range from in-depth explorations of Japan to journeys connecting the major cities and islands of Southeast Asia, with 14 overnight ports adding extra time ashore.

"Asia is one of those regions where you can experience something completely different from one port to the next, from a major city like Hong Kong to our new call at Coron in the Philippines, known for its turquoise waters and rich history," said Paul Grigsby, vice president of deployment and revenue planning for Holland America Line. "That contrast is what makes these itineraries so interesting to build. The new ports take guests beyond the places they may already know, introducing them to islands, coastlines and historic communities that reveal another side of the region, while natural phenomena like Japan's cherry blossoms can make the experience completely different depending on when you visit."

The five new ports add a mix of tropical landscapes, natural wonders and historic sites to the season.

  • Coron, Busuanga Island, Philippines, is known for the emerald Twin Lagoons.
  • Japan offers two new locales: Hirara introduces guests to the white-sand beaches and turquoise waters of Miyako Island, while Wakayama offers access to Wakayama Castle and the sacred mountain temples of Koyasan.
  • Magong showcases the striking basalt coastline of Taiwan's Penghu Island.
  • Muara provides a gateway to Brunei Darussalam and the gold-domed Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque.

Spring brings another reason to explore Japan as the country's famed cherry blossom season unfolds across different regions. Guests sailing spring itineraries can seek out the blooms along their journey, while those embarking in Tokyo can extend their stay before or after their cruise for more time to experience the season ashore. Shore excursions provide additional opportunities to take in the seasonal color, including from Kobe, where guests can visit UNESCO World Heritage-listed Himeji Castle and neighboring Koko-en Garden, known for its cherry blossoms in early spring.

More Time to Explore
Across the 2028-2029 Asia season, guests can enjoy overnight stays and late-night departures in 14 ports throughout the region. The additional time ashore creates a more relaxed pace, with opportunities to experience a city after dark, linger over dinner, revisit a favorite spot or take part in longer excursions. By extending time in port into the evening or the following day, guests can experience more of a destination's local culture, cuisine and nightlife without feeling rushed.

  • Overnight ports throughout Asia include Bali, Indonesia; Halong Bay, Vietnam; Hong Kong, China; Incheon (Seoul), South Korea; Keelung (Taipei), Taiwan; Laem Chabang (Bangkok), Thailand; Manila, Philippines; Hiroshima, Osaka and Maizuru, Japan; Phú Mỹ (Ho Chi Minh City) and Halong Bay, Vietnam; Shanghai, China; and Singapore. New overnight stays for the 2028-2029 season include Keelung and Phú Mỹ.
  • Guests can take advantage of extended stays by watching a sunset in Halong Bay, exploring Manila's historic San Agustin Church or experiencing Shanghai's neon city lights after dark.
  • Late-night departures also give guests additional time in Fukuoka, Hiroshima, Maizuru and Osaka, Japan; Halong Bay, Vietnam; and Shanghai, China.

Coffee, Tea and Spice Take Center Stage on New 27-Day Legendary Voyage
New for 2029, Holland America Line will introduce a 27-day Coffee, Tea & Spice Route Legendary Voyage aboard Eurodam, departing Jan. 3 roundtrip from Singapore. The itinerary visits 13 ports across seven countries, tracing the region's coffee, tea and spice traditions from Java and Manila to Taiwan and Hong Kong, with overnight calls in Bali, Hong Kong and  Phú Mỹ, the gateway to Ho Chi Minh City. On board, Holland America Line plans to bring the journey to life through regionally inspired tea and coffee experiences.

2028-2029 Asia Season Highlights

  • Circle Japan: 11- and 14-day itineraries sail roundtrip or between Tokyo and Yokohama (Tokyo), exploring ports throughout Japan and South Korea. The 14-day cruises visit up to 10 ports, with select extended calls in Hiroshima; the 11-day April 22, 2029, cruise features an overnight in Maizuru.
  • Japan & South Korea Discovery: Two 14-day cruises explore Japan and South Korea, with an overnight in Incheon (Seoul) and extended calls in Osaka and/or Fukuoka. The 11-day Southern Japan & Jeju Discovery, departing May 3, 2029, adds a call at Jeju.
  • Japan, Taiwan & China: The 14-day Japan & Taiwan cruise departs Nov. 5, 2028, from Tokyo to Hong Kong, with overnights in Osaka and Keelung (Taipei). A 14-day China & Japan Discovery departing Feb. 25, 2029, features overnights in Shanghai and Osaka.
  • Southeast Asia Discovery: The 14-day Nov. 19, 2028, sailing from Hong Kong to Singapore features overnights in Laem Chabang (Bangkok) and Halong Bay. A 17-day holiday itinerary departs Dec. 17, adding Nha Trang, Vietnam, and Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia, along with festive onboard programming.
  • Thailand & Philippines Discovery: The 14-day Dec. 3 sailing from Singapore to Hong Kong features six ports, including overnights in Laem Chabang (Bangkok) and Manila.
  • North Pacific Crossings: Two cruises connect Asia with the Pacific Northwest: a 13-day Vancouver-to-Tokyo crossing with Ketchikan, Alaska, and scenic cruising through the Inside Passage, and a 14-day Tokyo-to-Seattle crossing featuring Kushiro, Japan, and three Alaska ports.

Guests looking to spend even longer in the region can combine select back-to-back itineraries into Collectors' Voyages, extending their exploration across multiple countries and destinations.

Bringing Asia's Flavors On Board
Holland America Line's Destination Dining program brings the itinerary onboard, with menus inspired by the places guests visit. For the 2028-2029 Asia season, guests can sample flavors from throughout the region with dishes including Japanese rockfish and fresh sushi, Korean bibimbap with beef bulgogi, Thai mango sticky rice, Filipino chicken adobo, matcha lava cake, Indonesian coconut-filled pancakes and Vietnamese-style fresh spring rolls.

Have It All Early Booking Bonus
For a limited time, when guests book 2028-2029 Asia cruises with the Have It All premium package, the standard package amenities of shore excursions, specialty dining, a Signature Beverage Package and Surf Wi-Fi are included — plus the added perk of free prepaid crew appreciation, along with free upgrades to the Elite Beverage Package and Premium Wi-Fi. 

Guests can also take advantage of Holland America Line's Exclusive Mariner Society Early Booking Bonus. Mariner Society loyalty members can enjoy up to $400 onboard credit per stateroom. 

For more information about Holland America Line or to book a cruise, consult a travel advisor, call 1-877-SAIL HAL (877-724-5425) or visit hollandamerica.com. 

Find Holland America Line on Facebook, Instagram and the Holland America Blog. You can also access all social media outlets via the home page at hollandamerica.com.

About Holland America Line
Holland America Line has been exploring the world for more than 150 years with expertly crafted itineraries, extraordinary service and genuine connections to the destinations. Offering a perfectly-sized ship experience, its fleet of 11 vessels visits nearly 400 ports in 114 countries around the world and has shared the thrill of Alaska for more than 75 years — longer than any other cruise line. Savour the Journey isn't just a tagline, it's a reinforcement that the cruise line provides experiences too good to hurry through, connecting travelers to the world and each other. Award-winning enrichment programming, entertainment and cuisine that brings each locale on board, including a revolutionary Global Fresh Fish Program, put Holland America Line at the forefront of premium cruising. Holland America Line is part of Carnival Corporation, the world's largest cruise company with a portfolio of cruise lines operating in over 800 ports & destinations worldwide. data.title: My husband spent $80,000 on a boat, yet says my plans for a $100,000 pottery studio are irresponsible. Who's right?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'We have $2.9 million in retirement accounts and a paid-off house worth $900,000'

"My husband says that's too much to risk on something that may never turn a profit." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I'm 62, my husband is 65, and we've been married 31 years. We have $2.9 million in retirement accounts, a paid-off house worth $900,000, depending on the market, and very little debt. He retired last year. I now work part-time at a dental office, three days a week.

For 15 years I've wanted to open a small pottery studio. I've taken classes, sold mugs and planters at the Saturday market, and right now I throw on a wheel in our cold garage and pack everything away when I'm done.

There's a space near the old rail depot, about 900 square feet with a big front window, that would be perfect. Between the build-out, a kiln, wheels, insurance and a year of rent, I figure I'd need about $100,000.

My husband says that's too much to risk on something that may never turn a profit. He's afraid I'll keep pouring money into it if it struggles. He also brings up healthcare, inflation and one of us living to 95.

Three years ago he bought a boat for $80,000, then spent another $12,000 on a new motor and a fish finder. He barely used it after the first summer and finally sold it at a loss. He says that's different because he never claimed the boat would make money.

I'm not claiming the studio will make us rich either. I'd be happy if it paid for itself. I'm willing to write a real business plan, set a budget and agree on a number we're willing to lose. I'd even start smaller, though this space really is right. I haven't signed anything or spent a cent.

He says I'm proposing another job instead of retirement. To me, the work I choose is exactly what retirement should be. Am I being unrealistic about what $100,000 means for us? And how do two people decide what's a reasonable thing to spend on?

A 62-Year-Old Wife

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'I like the idea of a big return': My financial adviser wants me to invest $350,000 in a UAE data center. Is this risky?

Tell your husband that you're not giving up before you've even started.

Dear Wife,

From your letter, it doesn't sound like pottery is just a business for you.

For you, pottery is a passion, and it's important to have something you like doing in retirement. If you are going to choose to open a business, it should be something you will love because it won't always be easy, and you may need to rely on that bedrock of belief when the going gets tough. That's in addition to financial projections, advice from an accountant, knowing where you draw a hard line on the budget if sales dry up, and even a Plan B for the space.

I'm not going to tell you to open a business and spend $100,000, which could be a little on the high side, although you will know more when you compare this plan to similar-sized businesses and complete your due diligence. More important, I'm not going to tell you not to do it, and I don't think anyone else should, either, at least not without hearing you out, visiting the proposed site and, crucially, seeing your business plan. What stands out from your letter is your husband's immediate, possibly knee-jerk, opposition.

However, pointing out that he bought an $80,000 motorboat and ended up throwing good money after bad and selling it at a loss may be fair, but it doesn't help your cause. Yes, he decided to pursue something that he eventually tired of or decided wasn't worth all the hassle and expense. He's the one who apparently lost interest in a project after spending nearly six figures, not you. But it won't help to trade successes and failures in a tit-for-tat argument.

If a pottery studio is a vocation, you have earned the right to at least look into it.

It may be that you don't have to lease this building, as romantic as it sounds. You could rent a space at a retirement center or local school, at least initially, invest in the equipment to host pottery classes, build up word of mouth or an online presence and see how much demand is out there. That way, you won't be locked into a lease if the demand is not there. It will also help you envision what success means to you. Is it teaching a twice-weekly class? Or running a full-time studio?

You raise a great point when you say your retirement is not about doing nothing, or spending all of your time on the golf course or tennis court, or sitting in your garden reading - rather, it's about pursuing work that fulfills you. If pottery is a vocation for you, you have earned the right to at least look into it, given that you have worked for probably 40-plus years in jobs that helped you and your husband build a $2.9 million nest egg, even if those jobs were not your first choice.

For what it's worth, your business plan should include projected costs, including the lease, insurance, equipment, advertising, branding and marketing; projected revenue; the target market (there may be schools or senior centers nearby that would jump at the opportunity for their community to learn pottery); and, of course, the competition (find out if there are similar businesses in your area and, if so, how close they are and what they charge for classes).

Related: 'I don't want to die on the sales floor': I'm 67 and earn $19.50 an hour at a big-box store. When can I finally retire?

Running the numbers

You won't win this argument on statements that your husband is the proverbial pot calling the kettle black, and you may not "win" the argument at all. But you will lend more credence to your pottery studio idea through data. You have $2.9 million for retirement, a mortgage-free house worth $900,000, hardly any debt, a husband who has already retired, Social Security coming down the pike, and you continue to work part-time, although that may have to end if you set up this studio.

To put your small business in context: Startup costs of $100,000 represent 3.45% of your retirement account balance. That's not nothing, but neither is it an outrageous, extravagant risk, particularly given that this is an investment to further a pastime that brings you joy and, hopefully, makes money. What is your annual income now? What will it be in five years? What are your annual expenses? How much of your retirement is in traditional accounts versus Roth?

Another missing piece of this puzzle: Do you have a "fun money" account, an emergency fund or CDs or bonds to draw from? Otherwise, you would have to take this money from your investments. That would mean you need to take more than $100,000, because you would have to pay tax on the money you withdraw from a traditional IRA or 401(k). You would lose future investment returns (which you would ideally recoup, even if only in part, from your studio).

A $100,000 startup cost represents 3.45% of your retirement-account balance.

Tell your husband that you're not giving up before you've even started, just as you would not expect him to give up on a passion project without at least stress-testing the finances. The unspoken part of this conversation, particularly after his motorboat project, is hanging over you. It does not sound like you are asking him for permission, per se - rather, you are requesting his support, and I assume you have both contributed to your retirement fund, either as a corporate worker or a homemaker.

Agree on a maximum amount you can afford to lose on a studio. You will need working capital, particularly in the early stages, when you are building your reputation. This is an opportunity to step back and ask what you want from retirement. How do you want to spend your savings? What kind of issues require unanimous agreement? (Did you agree to the motorboat purchase, for instance?) How will you navigate such issues while respecting each other's space?

A woman named Kyla Glendenning opened up a pottery studio in Fort Lauderdale and said she had revenue of $71,000 in the first six months, but spent nearly $20,000 on Facebook advertisements. That tells me, in addition to the costs of setting up a studio, signing a lease and buying equipment, that your biggest challenges will be getting the word out that you exist. Her online tutorials and videos on social media - where I found her - also require both time and money.

Don't let anyone crack your bowls before they've even hit the kiln.

Related: My wife says we can't afford to retire. I vetoed her $8,000 trip to Italy. We're in our 60s and have $4 million. Do I keep working?
